name: TLL Capability Truth Matrix
description: Canonical capability matrix for TLL OS. Each capability has a claim, evidence, confidence, and last_verified date. This is the single source of truth for what TLL can and cannot do. Agents MUST query this file before claiming capabilities.

capabilities.name: Lexer and Parser
capabilities.claim: TLL can lex and parse TLL source code into AST.
evidence: self-hosting bootstrap: TLL compiler is written in TLL and compiles itself
CI Run #123 bootstrap step pass

capabilities.name: Compiler (TLL → Bytecode)
capabilities.claim: TLL compiler can compile TLL source to TLL bytecode (.tllbc).
evidence: self-hosting: compiler_self_compiled.tllbc exists
CI bootstrap step: TLL compiler compiles itself
capabilities.known_issue: P0-15.18.4 found and fixed codegen variable scope bug (non-main function let/const incorrectly falling back to global). Fixed in commit effe492. 10 scope tests (95 assertions) guard this.

capabilities.name: Virtual Machine
capabilities.claim: TLL VM can execute TLL bytecode.
evidence: all 34 tests pass on 3 platforms
blockchain 4-node network runs on VM

capabilities.name: Scope Semantics (function-level)
capabilities.claim: TLL uses function-level scope. Global/local variable isolation, shadowing, parameters, nested functions, closures, recursion, coroutines all work correctly.
evidence: 10 scope tests, 95 assertions, all pass
scope_01 through scope_10 cover global/local, shadowing, params, nested fn, closure, block scope, coroutine, recursion, return lifetime, complete chain

capabilities.name: Coroutine (100K stress verified)
capabilities.claim: TLL runtime supports 100K concurrent coroutines without crash, deadlock, or memory corruption.
evidence: coroutine_stress_test.tll: 100K immediate-return + 10K x 10 yield + 1K sleep, all pass
3 platforms: Ubuntu, Windows MSVC, macOS
CI Run #123 pass

capabilities.name: TCP Sockets
capabilities.claim: TLL runtime supports TCP client/server with non-blocking IO and select().
evidence: P2P 4-node network uses real TCP
blockchain tests use real TCP between independent processes
CI 3 platforms pass
capabilities.known_limitation: FD_SETSIZE=64. Maximum 64 concurrent file descriptors. Exceeding 64 results in silent ignore (no crash). This is a design limit, verified in P0-15.18.2.

capabilities.name: Long-Run Stability (120s verified)
capabilities.claim: TLL runtime can run 4-node blockchain network for 120 seconds with 20 blocks mined, stable RSS, no crash, no deadlock.
evidence: lrs_a/b/c/d.tll: 4 nodes, 120 seconds, Node A mines 20 blocks x 3tx, all nodes sync
CI Run #123 3 platforms pass
Max RSS Windows: 573MB
capabilities.note: 120 seconds is the verified duration. Longer durations (10+ minutes) are planned for future phases.

capabilities.name: Memory Safety (source-audited, runtime leak not verified)
capabilities.claim: TLL runtime has no obvious memory leaks in source code audit.
evidence: source code audit of vm.c, value.c, builtin.c found no obvious leaks
120s long-run test showed stable RSS
not_verified: ASAN/valgrind runtime leak detection has not been performed
coroutine object release after completion is not independently verified
frame/value reference counting edge cases not exhaustively tested
capabilities.planned_verification: Future phase will add ASAN build and valgrind leak detection.

capabilities.name: SHA-256
capabilities.claim: TLL supports SHA-256 hashing (pure TLL implementation).
evidence: stdlib/crypto.tll sha256() implementation
used by blockchain block hash, transaction hash, merkle root
crypto_vectors.tll test vectors pass

capabilities.name: HMAC-SHA256
capabilities.claim: TLL supports HMAC-SHA256 (pure TLL implementation).
evidence: stdlib/crypto.tll hmacSha256() implementation
used by blockchain SIMULATED signature
capabilities.note: HMAC is used as SIMULATED signature in blockchain. This is NOT real asymmetric cryptography.

capabilities.name: Ed25519 Asymmetric Signature
capabilities.claim: TLL supports Ed25519 key generation, signing, and verification.
capabilities.planned: P0-15.19 TLL Cryptographic Foundation will add C-native Ed25519 implementation.
capabilities.current_state: Blockchain uses HMAC-SHA256 as SIMULATED signature. Not real asymmetric cryptography.

capabilities.name: Secure Random Number Generator
capabilities.claim: TLL supports cryptographically secure random byte generation.
capabilities.planned: P0-15.19 will add C-native secure random (Linux: getrandom, Windows: BCryptGenRandom, macOS: /dev/urandom).

capabilities.name: SHA-512
capabilities.claim: TLL supports SHA-512 hashing.
capabilities.planned: P0-15.19 will add SHA-512 (C-native for Ed25519 internal use, pure TLL for stdlib API).

capabilities.name: 4-Node Blockchain Network (real TCP, real processes)
capabilities.claim: TLL can run a 4-node blockchain network with independent processes, real TCP, real P2P, transaction propagation, block propagation, and chain synchronization.
evidence: bc_node_a/b/c/d.tll: 4 independent processes, real TCP
bc_multi_a/b/c/d.tll: 5 consecutive blocks mined by different nodes
bc_sync_a/b.tll: auto sync on connect
CI 3 platforms pass, 15 blockchain network gates

capabilities.name: Transaction Propagation (120 tx high-message stress)
capabilities.claim: TLL blockchain can propagate 120 transactions from Node A to B/C/D with deduplication, mempool capacity=50 overflow/eviction, and block mining.
evidence: bc_stress.tll: 120 tx, mempool capacity=50, overflow eviction, 50-tx block mined
B/C/D max mempool=120 (strong evidence of receipt, verified in P0-15.18.3R)
CI 3 platforms pass

capabilities.name: Fault Injection (5 scenarios)
capabilities.claim: TLL blockchain handles duplicate tx, duplicate block, out-of-order block, kill-9 node restart, and multi-node consecutive faults.
evidence: fi_duptx.tll: duplicate transaction storm, deduplication works
fi_dupblock.tll: duplicate block storm, no duplicate insertion
fi_ooo.tll: out-of-order block, future block rejected, normal block accepted
fi_kill9.tll: kill -9 node, other nodes continue, restart node, reconnect, auto sync
fi_multi.tll: kill B, kill C, continue, restore B, restore C, all sync
CI 3 platforms pass, 15 fault injection gates

capabilities.name: Invalid Block Rejection
capabilities.claim: TLL blockchain rejects blocks with wrong hash, wrong prevHash, wrong index, invalid transactions, and invalid PoW.
evidence: bc_invalid_a/b.tll: invalid block scenarios, all rejected
handleBlockMessage validates index, previousHash, blockHash, transactions before adding to chain

capabilities.name: Fork Detection (detect and reject, no reorg)
capabilities.claim: TLL blockchain can detect competing chains (forks) and reject conflicting blocks.
evidence: forkCount tracking in handleBlockMessage
conflicting block at same height is rejected
not_implemented: Chain Reorg: cannot switch to a longer/heavier chain
Orphan Block Pool: future blocks are discarded, not buffered
Heaviest/Best Chain Selection: no cumulative work calculation
capabilities.note: Current implementation is '4-node replicated chain', not 'full blockchain consensus network'. Fork detection exists (reject conflict), but fork resolution (reorg) does not.

capabilities.name: Real Cryptographic Signatures
capabilities.claim: TLL blockchain uses real asymmetric cryptography (Ed25519) for transaction signatures.
capabilities.current_state: HMAC-SHA256 SIMULATED signature. Both signing and verification use tx.publicKey as HMAC key. This is explicitly noted in source code as SIMULATED.
capabilities.planned: P0-15.19 will upgrade blockchain signatures to Ed25519.

capabilities.name: Account State / Nonce / Balance
capabilities.claim: TLL blockchain has full account state management with nonce continuity, balance checking, and double-spend prevention.
capabilities.current_state: Mempool has duplicate detection by tx ID, but no account nonce state, no balance checking, no full double-spend prevention. Mempool has capacity, fee, expiration, sorting, eviction, nonce query.
capabilities.planned: Future phase (after P0-15.19) will add account state.

capabilities.name: Chain Persistence
capabilities.claim: TLL blockchain can persist chain state to disk and recover on restart.
capabilities.current_state: All chain state is in-memory. Node restart starts from genesis. Kill-9 test verifies restart + resync, but not persistence.
capabilities.planned: Future phase will add persistence (LevelDB or file-based).

capabilities.name: Truth Engine (machine-readable engineering truth)
capabilities.claim: TLL has a machine-readable truth engine that defines capabilities, evidence, and confidence levels.
evidence: .tll-engine/truth/ directory with architecture.json, language.json, runtime.json, capability.json
schema_version 1.0
each capability has claim, status, confidence, evidence, last_verified
capabilities.note: This is the bootstrap phase (P0-16.0). Structure and schema are established. Full automation (CI validation, auto-update, query API) is future work.

capabilities.name: Agent Development Protocol
capabilities.claim: TLL has a defined protocol for AI Agent participation in development.
evidence: .tll-engine/protocol/development.yaml, testing.yaml, audit.yaml
8-phase workflow: Identity → Truth → Plan → Code → CI → Evidence → Cognition → Verification
capabilities.note: Protocol is defined in v0.1. Enforcement via CI hooks is future work.

capabilities.name: Engineering Cognition Graph
capabilities.claim: TLL has a machine-readable engineering cognition graph that models dependencies, decisions, and evidence relationships.
evidence: .tll-engine/cognition/graph.json, dependency.json, decisions.json
capabilities.note: Graph structure is established. Population with full project data and query API is future work. NOT a neural network — it is a machine-verifiable engineering world model.

capabilities.name: Evidence System
capabilities.claim: TLL has a structured evidence system with provenance, hash, scope, and confidence.
evidence: .tll-engine/evidence/ directory with ci/, benchmark/, audit/ subdirectories
Evidence Schema defined in truth/capability.json
capabilities.note: Directory structure and schema are established. Automated evidence collection from CI is future work.

production_readiness.reason: TLL has strong verified capabilities in language core, runtime, coroutine, TCP, P2P, and blockchain network demo. However, it lacks real asymmetric cryptography, account state, persistence, chain reorg, and runtime memory safety verification. These are required for production-grade blockchain or secure systems.
